title.en: Bama: We Too Are Human Beings

hook.en: A grown man carries a small packet by its string as though it might bite him. Why would he hold food that way?

objectives.en: Narrate Bama's walk home from school
Describe Annan's advice and its effect

narration.en: A grown man carries a small packet by its string as though it might bite him. Why would he hold food that way?

body.en: Bama, in the third standard, takes a long time to walk home from school because she stops to watch everything: a performing monkey, a snake charmer, street sellers, a temple festival and the threshing of grain in the fields. The playful detail shows a curious, lively child who has not yet understood caste.

We trace how Bama moves from laughter to understanding.

title.en: The vadai incident and Annan's advice

body.en: She sees an elder of her community carrying a small packet of vadais by its string without touching it, bowing and handing it to the landlord. She finds it funny until her elder brother, Annan, explains that upper-caste people believe the touch of those from her community pollutes. Annan tells her that they must study and make progress, because education will earn them respect. Bama studies hard and stands first in her class.

points.en: Elder holds the packet by its string
Education as the way to respect

narration.en: She sees an elder of her community carrying a small packet of vadais by its string without touching it, bowing and handing it to the landlord. She finds it funny until her elder brother, Annan, explains that upper-caste people believe the touch of those from her community pollutes. Annan tells her that they must study and make progress, because education will earn them respect. Bama studies hard and stands first in her class.

problem.en: What advice did Annan give Bama, and how did she act on it?

steps.en: Annan explained that their people were denied respect.
He said education was the way to gain honour.
Bama studied hard and stood first in her class.

answer.en: Annan told Bama that their community was denied honour because of caste, but that by studying and making progress they could overcome this. Bama took his words to heart, studied very hard and stood first in her class.
